article.story: SOUTH BEND, Ind. -- — Braeden Shrewsberry scored 18 of his career-high 29 points in the second half to help Notre Dame pull away and beat Central Michigan 88-70 on Tuesday night. Shrewsberry finished 11 of 18 from the floor and made four of his six 3-pointers after halftime. Logan Duncomb added 20 points for Notre Dame (7-1), which has won three straight since its 86-78 loss to then-No. 1 Florida in the Players 8 tournament. Brady Koehler scored 18 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Fighting Irish. Braeden Smith added 15 points. Notre Dame used a 14-6 run for a 67-56 advantage with 8:15 to play. Central Michigan cut the deficit to 70-63, but the Fighting Irish scored the next five points and held a double-digit lead the rest of the way. Phat Phat Brooks scored 20 points to lead four in double-figure scoring for Central Michigan (4-3). Brooks had six of the Chippewas' 13 assists. Central Michigan closed the first half on a 7-2 spurt to trail 39-38 at the break. Shrewsberry scored 11 first-half points and Duncomb and Smith added 10 each for the Fighting Irish, who shot 39% but hit 6 of 12 from long range and all seven of their free-throw attempts. Brooks scored 11 in the first half to pace the Chippewas. It was the first meeting between the teams since a 69-68 road win by Central Michigan on Dec. 6, 2003. Notre Dame lead the series 3-1. Up next Central Michigan: at Miami (Ohio) on Dec. 2. Notre Dame: plays Stonehill on Saturday in the second of a program-record nine-game homestand. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
